lenses.label: SPHERE/ZIMPOL · polarised dust, 2024
lenses.title: Polarised dust around Betelgeuse in 2024
lenses.description: The degree of linear polarisation VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL measured in the V band on 3 December 2024, in the colour map and on the zero-to-0.10 scale the paper prints it in, placed in the plane of the sky through the star and spread along the line of sight by the scattering-angle efficiency of polarised light. The patches are dust. The colours are the publisher's legend for a ratio, not the colour of anything. Depth is a stated convention, not a measurement, and nothing finer than the 16 milliarcsecond beam is in the data.
lenses.summary: Measured polarised light from dust one to 4.5 stellar radii out; its depth is a fitted shell, not a measurement.

facts.label: Instrument
facts.value: VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL, V band, 3 December 2024

facts.value: 16 mas, 0.76 stellar radii

facts.label: Drawn extent
facts.value: 1 to 4.5 stellar radii, tapering to 6

facts.label: Colour scale

facts.label: Depth

lenses.label: Great Dimming clump · December 2019
lenses.title: The dust clump of the Great Dimming
lenses.description: The dust clump Montargès et al. fitted with RADMC-3D to the images of the Great Dimming, drawn from the numbers they published for December 2019: a sphere of uniform density south and slightly west of the star and between it and us. Its extinction is scaled so the line of sight through its centre dims the star ten times, as the paper reports for the southern hemisphere, and the light it scatters back is drawn faintly over that. This is a model fitted to images, not an image.
lenses.summary: The published model of the dust that dimmed the star ten times in December 2019, drawn as the extinction it causes.

facts.label: Model
facts.value: RADMC-3D sphere of constant density, Montargès et al. 2021, Extended Data Table 3

facts.value: (−1.9, −3.0, +12.5) au along right ascension, declination and toward Earth; radius 6.5 au

facts.label: Dust density
facts.value: 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ g cm⁻³ in MgFeSiO₄ grains centred on 0.21 µm

facts.label: Optical depth
facts.value: ln 10 through the centre, the 10-times dimming the paper reports

facts.label: Epoch
facts.value: December 2019, the only optimised solution the paper reports

lenses.label: VLTI/MATISSE · off-limb light, 2020
lenses.title: The light outside Betelgeuse’s disc at 4 micrometres
lenses.description: The same reconstruction that paints this star’s sphere carries a fifth of its flux outside the published disc. On the sphere that light is a flat plate behind the body; here it is given a shape. The disc and the first beam beyond it are removed, because inside the disc the sphere is drawn and within one beam of it the light is the star’s own edge smeared by the beam. What is left falls far too slowly to be that beam: the envelope that best projects to it is r^−7.9, five times better than the constant depth an extrusion assumes. The image spans 100 milliarcseconds, so this speaks for the inner envelope alone. Its colours are the reconstruction’s own heat scale, because this is the same quantity as the sphere.
lenses.summary: The fifth of the reconstruction that lies outside the disc, given the shape that best projects to it.

facts.label: Instrument
facts.value: VLTI/MATISSE, 3.94–4.00 µm, February 2020, 4 mas beam

facts.label: Drawn extent
facts.value: 1.19 to 2.36 stellar radii: outside the disc and its first beam, to the edge of the 100 mas field

facts.label: Share of the flux
facts.value: A fifth of the reconstruction lies outside the disc

facts.label: Colour scale
facts.value: The reconstruction's own heat scale, the one the star's sphere carries

facts.label: Depth
facts.value: Not measured; the steeply falling envelope r^−7.9 that best projects to the measured profile

lenses.label: ALMA · SiO envelope, August 2023
lenses.title: Silicon monoxide around Betelgeuse, placed by its own velocities
lenses.description: ALMA saw silicon monoxide around this star in August 2023, and this is the one dataset here whose depth comes from measured velocities rather than from a shape fitted to a picture. Measured from the star itself, found in the same observation’s continuum, the molecule absorbs in front of the star and glows in a lopsided ring 2.4 stellar radii out, heaviest to the east-south-east. Every channel of the line cube is placed along the line of sight on a spherical outflow at 22.0 kilometres a second, the speed of the fastest gas it absorbs in front of the star, the usual first reading of an expanding stellar envelope. The same absorption shows gas falling back as well, and that gas is placed as if it were flowing out. Silicon monoxide is what silicate dust condenses from, so this is the material of the other datasets caught before it became dust. The colours are a false-colour ramp for line brightness.
lenses.summary: Silicon monoxide around the star, placed in depth by its own measured velocities.

facts.label: Instrument
facts.value: ALMA band 6, SiO v=0 J=5–4 at 217.105 GHz, 3 to 27 August 2023, beam 30 × 22 mas
